messages:
Lee (customer): Hey, our private VPC service started failing after the midday cert rotation. Our SDK is throwing TLS errors on every request.
Sam (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact error your client sees? Also, are you hitting the VIP or an IP? :thinking:
Lee (customer): Error from our Go service:

```
2026-03-16T17:04:12Z rpc error: code = Unknown desc = x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

We call https://10.18.5.21:443 (internal proxy IP) because DNS was flaky earlier.
Anya (eng-sre): Important detail — calling by IP often breaks SNI. Can you try with the hostname you normally use (api.internal.example) and re-run `openssl s_client` with -servername to compare? Also, did you recently pin the cert bundle on your end?
Lee (customer): We pinned the CA bundle last month, but the error only started after rotation. Here's quick output from openssl (from our jump host):

```
# with -servername (works)
openssl s_client -connect api.internal.example:443 -servername api.internal.example
CONNECTED(00000003)
session_get_peer: peer: CN = api.internal.example
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.internal.example
---
# without -servername (shows old cert)
openssl s_client -connect 10.18.5.21:443
CONNECTED(00000003)
session_get_peer: peer: CN = old-default.example
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=old-default.example
```

Sam (support): That looks like SNI-dependent routing on our load balancer. If the client doesn't send server_name, the LB falls back to the default cert (old-default) which doesn't match your hostname => x509 error. @Anya can you confirm LB behavior for this VIP after rotation? rotator-bot just posted the rotation event earlier.
rotator-bot: rotation completed for cert-bundle-2026-03-16 at 2026-03-16T16:59:10Z, old cert moved to archive store.
Anya (eng-sre): Confirmed — our frontend ALB uses SNI to pick the listener cert. The new cert only has CN/SAN for api.internal.example; the LB default cert (served when SNI absent) is still old-default.example. If a client connects by IP or without SNI, it will receive the default cert.
Dmitri (infra): Root cause summary: customer was connecting to an IP (or their SDK stripped SNI) so post-rotation the presented default cert no longer matched their pinned name. Two remediation paths:
 - short-term: we can add api.internal.example as a SAN to the LB default cert so connections without SNI still validate (we can do this for a few hours during rollover).
 - recommended: have the customer update their client to use the hostname (not IP) or ensure the SDK sets TLS ServerName. Common culprits: older Go <1.8 or custom TLS wrappers that clear ServerName when dialing IP.
Anya (eng-sre): Quick repro steps for customer SDKs (shareable):

1) Verify SNI with openssl from their environment:
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.18.5.21:443 -servername api.internal.example
```
Expect new cert with CN=api.internal.example.

2) Check client behavior by attempting a curl request to IP with Host header and with hostname:
```
curl -v --resolve api.internal.example:443:10.18.5.21 https://api.internal.example/health
curl -v https://10.18.5.21/ -H 'Host: api.internal.example'
```
Note: curl sets SNI when the URL host is a name; connecting directly to IP may not set SNI.

3) For Go, ensure tls.Dial or http.Transport uses ServerName (set TLSClientConfig.ServerName if needed).

Sam (support): Lee — can you check whether your service is dialing the IP (10.18.5.21) programmatically? If so, can you switch to the hostname and test? If you can't change the client quickly, we can apply the TEMP fallback on our side.
Lee (customer): We are dialing IP because of an internal resolver bug. We can push a hotfix to switch to hostname but that will take ~2 hours. Could you enable the fallback SAN for the default cert while we patch? :pray:
Dmitri (infra): We can add a SAN to the default cert as a short-lived workaround. I'll coordinate with certops — ETA 30-45m. We'll mark it for rollback after your patch is deployed. Also adding a note in the rotation playbook to validate default-cert coverage for IP->hostname drift.
Anya (eng-sre): Also adding this to the incident: recommend we update docs with a callout: "Do not connect by IP to hostnames that rely on SNI; if unavoidable, ensure the client's TLS stack sets ServerName."
Lee (customer): Thanks all — we'll roll the client fix and confirm. Will post results here.
Sam (support): Thanks. If you can paste a small tcpdump showing the TLS ClientHello from your process (wireshark/tcpdump with -w) we can validate the absence/presence of the SNI extension. Example filter: `tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/sni.pcap host 10.18.5.21 and port 443`.
Lee (customer): Will do. Update incoming in ~1.5h.
Anya (eng-sre): Great. Marking this thread as investigation + workaround planned. :white_check_mark:
